# LowerOrderGenerator: design history

How the large classes got their current shape: decisions, found-and-fixed bugs, rejected designs, comments that disagreed with the code. Of interest when changing an old decision; the current behaviour is in the reference docs next to this file.

## AddressLoweringPass

- Design of the `$offset`/size format: the goal was that a name stops being a name and becomes an address relative to the base pointer.
- `offset` kept signed (not a bare magnitude) because parameters on the caller's stack will need positive offsets later.
- ADDR of an unresolved name (`ALLOC_STATIC`, top-level `GLOBAL`) originally left the entire line unrewritten (full canonical type text). It was documented as a "Known gap", but it was a found-and-fixed inconsistency: all real ADDR emission sites pass a bare name (checked by grep), so the case is just "not a stack local", and it now gets `ADDR size name`, as an unresolved PUSH does. Verified against a `let static x = mut 0` fixture. `GT_DESTRUCT`'s dotted-chain gap is different and still open.
- `RET_FLOAT`/`PUSH_RET_FLOAT`: a new mnemonic was accepted because the float/int return register distinction cannot be carried by existing operands; precedent: `CAST` split, `IN`/`IN_SCAN`, `LEN`/`LEN_SCAN`. The actual rule is "don't invent a mnemonic for what operands could already say".
- `RETURNS` dropped once RET carries the byte count.
- LOOKUP: the earlier description of `LOOKUP_DYN` as "one pointer indirection through an 8-byte heap-buffer handle" was a design bug, found wrong because every `resize` call site re-`POP`s the returned address into the same variable (a handle layer would make that unnecessary). A dynarray is a plain 8-byte pointer with a `+8` header offset. There used to be a `LOOKUP_SLICE` mnemonic; removed with the slice type.
- Comparison split (`_INT`/`_FLOAT`) came first with the four ordered compares, `EQ`/`NEQ` were added right after. AND/OR were first made size-only; ADD/SUB/MUL/DIV/MOD were first size-only too, then corrected to the `_INT`/`_FLOAT` split in the same session. INC/DEC got the split for consistency ("architecture independent, but better done than not done"); `DEC` and the `--` operator were added to the compiler in the same change.
- `NEW_DYN size`: explicit decision NOT to fold the 8-byte safe length header into `size`.
- `NEW size` first looked like it also served `dyn([...])` with three operands; that was split off into `NEW_DYN`/`NEW_UDYN`.
- `URESIZE` has a safe-type fallback only for `CloneGenerationPass.buildCloneLoop`.
- `POP` was first only for call-argument transfer (`POP ARGn size`); widened to a general "pop into named local" when `MembershipLoweringPass` needed it for non-simple `IN` left operands.
- A flattened pointer-chain name ("Known gap" in `resolveAddress`) is closed on the compiler side (`isQualifiedNameableDot` decides per level); the bail remains as a safety net for unaudited callers.
- ADDR_OF drop: the check used to be "the preceding line's trailing type carries ANY storage". That also matched `raw val`/`auto val` of a pointer-typed local and caused a real segfault (null `MEMCOPY` destination). Narrowed to `opText` REF/RAW.
- `IN`/`WITHIN` lowering and `GT_LOOP`/`CLONE_LOOP`: originally planned to reach this pass as new mnemonics for a not-yet-built codegen; both passes were rebuilt to emit ordinary JMP/CMP loops inline, so they never arrive.
- Top-level `GLOBAL` rewrite was missing at first (globals passed through untouched after `ALLOC_STATIC` had already been switched); found and fixed.
- Struct/enum declaration lines dropped on request ("can we remove struct and enum definitions from the lower order output now?") once all uses were spent.
- Single combined `ALLOC` (the sum of all local slots) replaced per-local ALLOC lines; frame total rounded UP to 16 (never down). Per-variable alignment was added as a companion to the compiler-side struct-padding round.
- The sibling-scope same-name slot reuse fix (see "Frame layout" in the ref) was added after wider stores spilled into neighbouring slots.
- Dropped as stale: references to the sibling `caspien-compiler` project and "not-yet-built codegen stage" wording (Codegen exists now); "(unclear)" whether the "ARG-to-ALLOC lowering" register/stack question is still open: kept as stated in the ref.
- Comment-vs-code: the `run()` comment said `previousLine` is not updated for `RETURNS`/decorators; the code matches (they `continue` before the update).

## History from AddressLoweringPass chunk 2

- `RET` split into `RET`/`RET_FLOAT` (and `PUSH_RET` into `_INT`/`_FLOAT`) because a bare byte count cannot say which register class carries the value; same precedent as the compiler-side `CAST` split. `f64` extends `isFloatBaseType` only, no `RET_FLOAT_64`.
- Comparisons were split into `_INT`/`_FLOAT` by owner request; `EQ`/`NEQ` were added right after the first four. Logical `AND`/`OR`, `NOT` and the `bits_*` ops deliberately have no such split (same machine operation at any width, integers only).
- `NOT` and `CLONE` lowering were added on request after a demo showed `CLONE` was emitted bare, with no type operand unlike every other mnemonic; the compiler now emits its operands in the standard style and this pass reduces them to `CLONE size`.
- `NEW` once covered the `dyn([...])` three-operand form too; that moved to its own `NEW_DYN`/`NEW_UDYN` mnemonics (for the same reason `LOOKUP` split: safe and unsafe dynarrays need different allocation shapes).
- `NEW_DYN size` deliberately excludes the length header: the owner said not to fold the 8 bytes in. Whether `NEW_DYN` itself writes the count into the header was left open at the time; `count` is kept on the line so it need not be derived by dividing back (rule: do not recover a value from the previous line).
- Bug found and fixed (LOOKUP): an unsafe dynarray fell through `lookupMnemonicFor` (its `unsafe_dynarray(` prefix matched neither the fixed-array nor the dynarray check), so `LOOKUP`/`LOOKUP_LHS` into one stayed unrewritten to the end of the pipeline (seen with `unsafe_dynarray_construct_test.caspien`, `arr[0]`, `arr[0] = 99`). Fixed with `unsafeDynArrayElementTypeOf`, routed to `LOOKUP_ARRAY`.
- Design correction (LOOKUP_DYN): it was once documented/implemented as one pointer indirection through a separate 8-byte handle. Wrong, because every `resize` call site re-assigns the returned address to the same variable (also `CloneGenerationPass.buildCloneLoop`); a handle layer would make that pointless. A dynarray is a plain pointer; only the header offset differs.
- A third `LOOKUP_SLICE` shape (origin resolved, "start" bound added) was removed together with the slice type.
- Bug found and fixed (statics): the first version of the `ALLOC_STATIC` size rewrite missed top-level `GLOBAL` lines (`let static counter = ...` still showed `GLOBAL counter mut_u64 0`), because `run` handed only in-function lines to `tryRewrite`. Hence the standalone `rewriteStaticOrGlobalDecl`, called for top-level lines too.
- Bug found and fixed (STACK_LOCK): the `___type` check used `members.get(members.size()-1)` (a leftover from before the "___type must be first" change, same as in `CloneGenerationPass.emitMemberPushSequence`); never noticed because nothing exercised STACK_LOCK on a class-id-bearing struct with several members. It now checks index 0. Padding: `sizeOf` includes `STRUCT_PADDING` gaps, so no separate fix was needed there.
- Bug found (retag): a broader "any storage at all" version of the `isAlreadyCorrectPointerRetag` check caused a real bug (details at the call site, not in this chunk).
- Param loading: `emitParamLoads` once distinguished register from stack words itself; now the emission is uniform and this pass decides. `resolveArgWordSlots` replaced line-by-line deciding once int and float words could interleave in a parameter list.
- `isFloatBaseType` had its Javadoc glued in front of `isSignedIntBaseType` (two Javadocs in a row); the stale text said "f32 only, today" while the code accepts f64 too. Trusted the code.
- Dropped as stale: the `STACK_LOCK` comment's claim that sizeOf is "now" the padded total (kept as present-tense fact); the `LOOKUP_DYN` "+8" header offset in comments, while CLAUDE.md says the safe header is 16 bytes (`[len][cap]`). The offset is applied outside this chunk; not verified here.
- Unclear: the comment on `findNewRunStart` return (`j - 1`) says it keeps the exclusive lower bound below the push; kept in code.

- DEREF: originally nothing carried the pointee size. Decision: the pointee type rides on the `DEREF` line itself rather than being inferred from the previous `PUSH` (a general principle for these passes: avoid reading it from the previous line where possible), mirroring `CLONE`.
- DEREF size: an earlier version (and `CLONE`'s rewrite still) explicitly stripped storage and then sized the bare base type. That only matched while operands were storage-free; `BytecodeEmitter.emitDot`'s storage-bearing-field case was the first to need the storage-bearing form, so `DEREF` now calls `sizes.sizeOf` directly (identical output for old callers).
- NEG: decision to drop `returnType` was checked against `checkUnaryMinus` (unsigned maps to signed of the same width).
- Arithmetic: first decided as plain size (like AND/OR), corrected to the `_INT/_FLOAT` split shortly after, on the "architecture independent, better done than not done" reasoning. Same for INC/DEC. `DEC` was added as a new mnemonic together with this rewrite (`emitDecrement`).
- ATOMIC_SWAP: reading size from `leftType` was a trap (the `atomic_` segment made the base parse as `atomic_char` and size as 8); found against fixture `atomic_swap_global_scalar_cg_test.caspien`. Size comes from the last operand.
- SEXT/ZEXT: verified against `cast_within_split_manual_check_test.caspien` (`SEXT mut_s8 mut_s32`, `ZEXT mut_u8 mut_u32`).
- RECURSIVE_CALL/EXTERN_CALL: both become `CALL`. EXTERN_CALL's `argCount` deliberately kept (varargs); dropping it for non-vararg externs by cross-referencing the EXTERN declaration (as was done for `RETURNS` once `RET`/`RET_FLOAT` made it redundant) is separate follow-up work, not done.
- ADDR: its unresolved-name case once bailed out and left the whole original line untouched (full canonical type text), e.g. `ADDR x mut_u64` for `let static x = mut 0` next to an already-lowered `PUSH 8 x`. Fixed to the uniform `ADDR size name`. An older doc comment called this a "Known gap"; it never was one for ADDR (no emission site builds a dotted string for it; verified by grepping every `ADDR ` emission). The "Known gap" applies to `GT_DESTRUCT` dotted chains through a pointer.
- MEMCOPY / NEW_FROM_STRING: considered keeping sizes ("MEMCOPY 8 8 8 8"), rejected as constant dead text.
- `memberLocOf`: originally summed `Member` sizes (`pseudoMembersOf`), which was wrong after `BytecodeEmitter.emitStruct` started baking padding in; now walks `LayoutEntry`. The `___type` special case was added so `instanceof`/`implements` lowering works on interface types.
- `pseudoLayoutOf` once also synthesized a slice's three-member layout; the slice type was removed from the language.
- `SizeCalculator.structSizeOf` was a plain member sum that ignored alignment/padding (a long-flagged gap); now layout-based. The bare-struct-name check in `sizeOf` was added after a generic instantiation (`HashMapEntry_u64`) was silently sized 8 instead of 32.
- Register-transferred params: the raw digit is rewritten to the per-bank index because independent-counting conventions (SysV/arm64) interleave int and float words (see `resolveArgWordSlots`).
- Dropped as stale: the comment on in-function ALLOC says "any more" history only; the unresolved-pointer comment in `resolveAddress` says the fallback is "no longer expected to fire".

## MembershipLoweringPass

- WITHIN was originally left unhandled (listed under "Known gaps") on the theory that strict-subset semantics were more complex than a bounds check. Once IN's range-vs-range subset test and the range-vs-dynarray shape existed, it turned out WITHIN needs the same materialize/dereference machinery plus a different final formula. The first WITHIN handling was scrapped and rebuilt on top of IN's machinery (owner direction).
- That change retired the compiler-side `PTR_WITHIN` mnemonic: it existed only because the compiler had to choose a mnemonic by operand pointerness before this pass had its own dereference step. IN never needed a `PTR_IN` for the same reason.
- Complex left operand of IN (call result, arithmetic, non-name LOOKUP) was a gap, closed by materializing into a `$in_tmpN` temp via a widened `POP` (previously `AddressLoweringPass`'s `POP` resolved only `ARGn` slots). Design principle from the owner: an instruction should rely on what is on the stack, not on what the most recent instruction was; temps are acceptable. `ASSIGN` was rejected for this because it needs the destination pushed first.
- Right-operand materialization bug: with a multi-line right operand (CALL = 4 lines), `outSoFar.size()-2` pointed mid-way into right's span; the first attempt produced a wrong double-POP (materialized garbage instead of `x` for `x in makeArr()`). Fix: if right is not simple, always materialize left too, never inspect it.
- Pointer-typed right operand of `u64 in range/dynarray` (`raw range(...)`, `raw dynarray(...)`) was an original known gap (`PUSH p.start`/`LEN` ran on the pointer's own address); fixed by dereferencing first with `PUSH / DEREF / POP` into a storage-free temp.
- `DEREF` used to carry no operand; a deref is a copy and needs a byte count, so it now carries the pointee type (found later, fixed with a real deref being a copy; see `derefInto`).
- `isGenuinePointer` bug: the first gate was `storage != null`, which wrongly dereferenced every ordinary dynarray (dynarrays always carry `owns` storage). Found by the first fixture using a plain local dynarray as the right operand. The `ref`-to-dynarray exception in the current code was added later (the code, not an old comment, is the source).
- Left-operand shape guard for IN: originally every left shape reached the plain-`u64` logic, so a 16-byte range left was compared with a same-sized `GT_EQ_INT`/`LT_INT` against a scalar bound (wrong bytecode, fixture `in_operator_range_range_test`). A guard (owner: "if its not a u64 on the left it should remain unhandled") was added first, then the dedicated subset and dynarray-check builders (Shape 4).
- `r in dynarray` uses `<=`, not `<` (confirmed: `N < N` would reject the range that exactly covers the array).
- Bare `range` narrow-check bug: recognition of ranges only accepted `range(` text; fixed first at the `r is base` rewrite, then missed in IN Shape 2/3 and the two WITHIN gates until caught against `for i in range(dynarray)` output. The WITHIN gap was the "WITHIN's incomplete-range case" noted in the X86Backend class comment as needing a fix in the lower-order generator; fixed at the root.
- IS_BASE: `leftType` was first read from `leftPush`'s trailing token, wrong for an inline range literal (two scalar pushes, trailing token `u64`). Fixed by writing the operand type on the `IS_BASE` line. The first `r is base` fixture also failed to match at all because a `@recursive` range parameter is pushed as bare `imut_range`. Side note: a separate request to remove the `debug()` keyword/builtin was done elsewhere (BytecodeEmitter/TypeChecker/Lexer/Parser); IS_BASE was only investigated alongside a leftover DEBUG mnemonic search.
- IN_SCAN: the owner suggested lowering `u64 in string` using `strlen()`; refined to a plain forward scan with no `strlen` call and no known length (same semantics and NUL caveat).
- IN_SCAN string dereference bug: using `isGenuinePointer` on a string literal (`static_some_imut_string`) wrongly dereferenced it (`PUSH string_id1 / DEREF`). Fixed by the `!"static".equals(storage)` gate, alongside a `CanonicalType` doc fix.
- LEN_SCAN added right after IN_SCAN shipped, once the `LOOKUP`/`LOOKUP_DYN` addressing fix (the "handle indirection" design bug in LOOKUP_DYN, in the project CLAUDE.md) made `LOOKUP` into an unsafe dynarray's elements resolve correctly. Owner's remark behind that fix: the base + 8 + index*width layout question for safe vs unsafe dynarrays needed a comprehensive fix.
- INSTANCEOF/IMPLEMENTS originally required a simple-push left and bailed otherwise (correct but unoptimized, e.g. `makeSub() instanceof Base`); extended to materialize like IN. Reason given: instanceof/implements were done before the IN work and did not reflect it.
- `typeFieldPathFor` bug: dotted `leftName.___type` against a storage-qualified local (`let sAuto = mut auto s; sAuto instanceof Base`, and any struct-returning call) was left unresolved in the final bytecode; fix is to deref first.
- `leftType` for INSTANCEOF/IMPLEMENTS: first version read the preceding line's trailing token, wrong for a bare non-`new` struct literal; now written on the operator line.
- Interface-typed left of instanceof/implements was first rejected (`members == null`); owner direction: the generator should not care whether the left is struct- or interface-typed, it is just a pointer to get `___type` from. Rejection removed.
- `IMPLEMENTS` with zero implementers: confirmed reachable from real source (a declared-but-unimplemented interface), lowered to constant false; the pass is deliberately silent, the warning lives in `checkImplementsOperator`.
- `isRealNameToken` (replaced shape-only `isSimplePush`/`isBarePush`): shape alone misfired on inline range literals `2..5`. First version rejected a leading `$`, which wrongly treated `PUSH $for_range_1 ...` as not simple and forced needless temps; this exposed the latent `allocInsertIndex` bug (header scan did not skip `ARG`/`EXPORT`, so a temp ALLOC could land mid-parameter-list and `ArgToAllocLoweringPass` left the remaining ARGs unlowered). Seen in stdlib functions with `ARG` parameters containing a `for` loop (`stdlib/gt/ghost_table.caspien`, `gt_alive_check.caspien`). Both were fixed together; the second would have appeared independently the next time a temp was needed in an ARG-bearing function.
- Disagreements noted: the old header said only `tryRewriteInScan` needs labels; `tryRewriteLenScan` also uses `newLabel` (the code is the truth). The old header and `buildRangeSubsetCheck` doc called WITHIN "still unhandled"; it is handled (`tryRewriteWithin`). The old header's "Known gaps" bullets (pointer right operand, range-left, non-simple operands, `u64 in string`) all describe closed gaps; instanceof/implements left must be a simple push -- no longer true (see above).
- Dropped as stale: the Known-gaps statement that a struct-typed left of instanceof/implements must still be a simple push, and the "pointer-typed right operand is a gap" framing.
